tone_statements.citation: Martin, Marieke. n.d. Wawa ideophone phonetics vs. Wawa phonology - language symbolism as addition or contrary. Conference talk abstract (venue and year not stated on the record), posted under 'Talks' on the author's Academia.edu profile, academia.edu/15329050.
tone_statements.quote: In Wawa, ideophones are usually easily recognisable for their preference of rare phonemes (e.g. labial-velar stops), their preference of high (1) and low (4) tones and 1-4 and 4-1 contours (in a 4-level tone system), and for featuring consonants in positions not normally allowed in the phonology of other Wawa words. This includes for example word-final sibilants, which are prominent in ideophones, but not found elsewhere in the Wawa lexicon. Generally, in the Wawa lexicon, contour tones are very common and all combinations exist, except 1-3 and 3-1.
tone_statements.locator: abstract, first paragraph (Talks section of the archived profile page)
tone_statements.summary: Four contrastive tone levels (numbered 1 high to 4 low) with very frequent contour tones (all two-level combinations except 1-3 and 3-1), lexical; ideophones favour the extreme levels and 1-4/4-1 contours. Note PHOIBLE's coding of Martin 2012 lists only three level tones (H, M, L).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1993. An outline classification of the Mambiloid languages. Journal of West African Languages 23(1): 105–118. (image scan from rogerblench.info via the Internet Archive; scanned at 300 dpi)
sources.note: §2.2 'Tone' (p. 111): 'Although no overall statement about tone in Mambiloid is yet possible, the group is exceptional for the complexity of its tonal systems and the prevalence of phonemic contour tones' (Vute 3 levels + 8 glides, Kwanja 3 levels, Mambila 4 levels). Wawa treated as the most divergent dialect of Vute (after Guarisma 1987). Nothing on stress; nothing Wawa-specific on prosody.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory GM 1647 'Wawa' (contributors Christopher Green & Steven Moran), source: Martin 2012, A grammar of Wawa (PhD, Kent).
sources.note: Segment inventory only (49 segments) including three tone segments: high (˦), mid (˧), low (˨) — i.e. Martin 2012 as coded by PHOIBLE treats Wawa as a three-level tone language; nothing about stress.
